categories.csv-structure: a comma inside a quoted CSV field
categories.delimiter-mix: values that combine another delimiter character (; tab |) with quotes, written quoted and unquoted; reviewed instead of failed when shell-metachar or quotes is under review
categories.duplicate: a value copied from another row (duplicate keys)
categories.file-structure: the sample itself, a header-only file, and CRLF line endings
categories.null-column: every value in one column empty (NULL once loaded into SQL)
categories.numeric-format: integers, decimals, signs, exponents, underscores, leading zeros, rounding edges
categories.pairs: two rows of the same group, each with an unusual value (sub-cent amounts, precision edges, another case), so the two values are combined
categories.quotes: single and double quotes inside values
categories.schema: an extra column (including each column that is new in the incident file) and reordered columns
categories.whitespace: leading, trailing, repeated and tab whitespace

limitations: Evidence covers only the input categories fixwitness generated; inputs outside them were not tested.
This is differential testing, not a formal proof of equivalence.
Attack checks use built-in payloads (command/code injection, path traversal, template injection); other vulnerability classes are not tested.
Scripts ran on this machine in temporary directories (process isolation, not a sandbox).
